content: Magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) is regarded as the most effective noninvasive diagnostic tool for detecting liver fibrosis, particularly in its early stages. However, the widespread use of MRE is limited due to its high cost and restricted accessibility. Although liver biopsy remains the gold standard for diagnosing nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), it is typically reserved for cases where other noninvasive diagnostic methods yield inconclusive results. This is because liver biopsy carries inherent risks and is associated with significant costs. In 2020, the American Gastroenterological Association, in collaboration with the American Diabetes Association (ADA), conducted a review of existing clinical guidelines. They subsequently proposed risk stratification algorithms aimed at optimizing the management of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and NASH in patients with diabetes.
